The Hare Krishna Heritage Tower is a religious and cultural skyscraper currently under construction in the Narsingi area of Hyderabad, India. Upon completion, the structure is projected to reach a height of approximately 430 feet (131 meters), making it one of the tallest religious buildings in the country. The project is being developed by the Hare Krishna Movement (HKM) Hyderabad.
History and construction
The foundation stone for the project was laid on May 8, 2023, by the then Chief Minister of Telangana, K. Chandrashekar Rao. During the ceremony, the state government announced a contribution of ₹25 crore toward the project's construction.
On August 25, 2024, the Anantha Sesha Sthapana ceremony was conducted to mark a milestone in the foundation works. The event was attended by the current Chief Minister of Telangana, A. Revanth Reddy. As of March 2026, construction is ongoing at the six-acre site.
Architecture and facilities
The design of the tower incorporates architectural elements from regional historical dynasties, including the Dravidian and Kakatiya styles. The structure is planned to house several shrines, including those dedicated to Sri Sri Radha Govinda Dev  and Sri Sri Sita Rama  Swamy.
The complex is expected to include:
* A library and digital research center for Vedic studies.
* An Annadhanam (food distribution) hall with the capacity to serve 500 people per session.
* A multi-vision theater and an interactive Bhagavad Gita exhibition.
* A guest house and cultural education center.
